results.title: Unitary reduction of a complex matrix to rectangular diagonal form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every rectangular complex matrix becomes rectangular diagonal after a unitary change of basis on the right, with a further unitary change of basis on the codomain (S. Axler, Linear Algebra Done Right, 4th ed., Section 7E).

results.title: Complex SVD with nonincreasing singular values
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: This is the rectangular complex SVD with singular values in nonincreasing order.

results.title: Squared Frobenius norm as the sum of squared singular values
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Frobenius-norm identity for an SVD: the sum of the squared singular values is the sum of the squared norms of the entries.

results.title: Singular value decomposition of a complex matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Rectangular complex singular value decomposition: every complex `m × n` matrix factors as `U * Σ * Vᴴ` with `U` and `V` unitary and `Σ` rectangular diagonal with nonnegative entries; the singular values beyond the first `min m n` (indices `j` with `m ≤ j.val`) are zero.

results.title: Singular value decomposition of a complex square matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a square complex matrix whose rows and columns are indexed by a finite type $n$. Then there are unitary matrices $U$ and $V$ and nonnegative real numbers $\sigma_i$ for $i \in n$ such that, writing $D$ for the diagonal matrix with diagonal entries $\sigma_i$ and $V^*$ for the conjugate transpose of $V$, we have $A = U D V^*$.

results.title: Orthogonal reduction of a real matrix to rectangular diagonal form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a real $m \times n$ matrix. Then there are orthogonal matrices $U$ of size $m \times m$ and $V$ of size $n \times n$ and real numbers $\sigma_1 \ge \sigma_2 \ge \dots \ge \sigma_n \ge 0$ with $\sigma_j = 0$ for every $j > m$, such that $AV = U\Sigma$, where $\Sigma$ is the $m \times n$ matrix with $\Sigma_{jj} = \sigma_j$ for $j \le \min(m, n)$ and all other entries zero.

results.title: Real singular value decomposition with nonincreasing singular values
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a real $m \times n$ matrix. Then there are orthogonal matrices $U$ of size $m \times m$ and $V$ of size $n \times n$ and real numbers $\sigma_1 \ge \sigma_2 \ge \dots \ge \sigma_n \ge 0$ with $\sigma_j = 0$ for every $j > m$, such that $A = U \Sigma V^{\mathsf{T}}$, where $\Sigma$ is the $m \times n$ matrix with $\Sigma_{jj} = \sigma_j$ for $j \le \min(m, n)$ and all other entries zero.

results.title: Real singular value decomposition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a real $m \times n$ matrix. Then there are orthogonal matrices $U$ of size $m \times m$ and $V$ of size $n \times n$ and real numbers $\sigma_1, \dots, \sigma_n \ge 0$ with $\sigma_j = 0$ for every $j > m$, such that $A = U \Sigma V^{\mathsf{T}}$, where $\Sigma$ is the $m \times n$ matrix with $\Sigma_{jj} = \sigma_j$ for $j \le \min(m, n)$ and all other entries zero.

results.title: The only biunitary triperfect number divisible by $27$ is $2160$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every positive integer $N$ divisible by $27$, $\sigma^{**}(N) = 3N$ if and only if $N = 2160$, where $\sigma^{**}$ is the biunitary divisor sum.

results.title: Parity of the biunitary divisor sum
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every positive integer $n$, the biunitary divisor sum $\sigma^{**}(n)$ is odd if and only if $n = 2^k$ for some natural number $k$ (so $n = 1$ is included).

results.title: Powers of two dividing the biunitary divisor sum of an odd number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every odd natural number $n$, $2^{\omega(n)}$ divides $\sigma^{**}(n)$, where $\omega(n)$ is the number of distinct prime factors of $n$ and $\sigma^{**}$ is the biunitary divisor sum.

results.title: Divisibility of the biunitary divisor sum of an even number by a power of two
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every positive even natural number $n$, writing $\omega(n)$ for the number of distinct prime factors of $n$, the power $2^{\omega(n) - 1}$ divides the biunitary divisor sum $\sigma^{**}(n)$.

results.title: Lower bounds for the biunitary divisor sum of a prime power
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $e \ge 1$, and write $\sigma^{**}$ for the biunitary divisor sum. Then, in $\mathbb{Q}$, $\sigma^{**}(p^e)/p^e \ge 1 + 1/p^2$; if moreover $e \ne 2$, then $\sigma^{**}(p^e)/p^e \ge 1 + 1/p$; and if $e \ge 3$, then $\sigma^{**}(p^e)/p^e \ge (1 + 1/p)(1 + 1/p^3)$.

results.title: Comparison bounds for the biunitary divisor sum of a prime power
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $m \ge 1$ and $e \ge 2m - 1$ be natural numbers, and write $\sigma^{**}$ for the biunitary divisor sum. Then, in $\mathbb{Q}$, $\sigma^{**}(p^e)/p^e \ge \sigma^{**}(p^{2m})/p^{2m}$, and if moreover $e \ne 2m$, then $\sigma^{**}(p^e)/p^e \ge \sum_{i=0}^{m} 1/p^i$.

results.title: Primitive prime divisors of $a^n - 1$ are $1$ modulo $n$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a \ge 2$ and $n \ge 2$ be natural numbers, and let $p$ be a primitive prime divisor of the integer sequence $m \mapsto a^m - 1$ at index $n$, that is, a prime that divides $a^n - 1$ and divides no $a^m - 1$ with $1 \le m < n$. Then $p \equiv 1 \pmod n$.

results.title: Primitive prime factors of $a^n + 1$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a \ge 2$ and $n \ge 1$ be integers with $(a, n) \ne (2, 3)$, and if $n = 1$ suppose that $a + 1$ is not a power of $2$. results.title: A Fourier coefficient is bounded by the L¹ norm
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T > 0$, let $\mu$ be the Haar probability measure on the circle $\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$, and let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{C}$. For every function $f : \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z} \to E$ and every $n \in \mathbb{Z}$, the $n$-th Fourier coefficient $\hat f(n) = \int e^{-2\pi i n t / T} f(t)\,d\mu(t)$ satisfies $\|\hat f(n)\| \le \int \|f(t)\|\,d\mu(t)$.

results.title: Riemann–Lebesgue for continuous functions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T > 0$ and let $\mu$ be the Haar probability measure on the circle $\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$. For every continuous function $g : \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{C}$, the Fourier coefficients $\hat g(n) = \int e^{-2\pi i n t / T} g(t)\,d\mu(t)$ tend to $0$ as $|n| \to \infty$, that is, along the cofinite filter on $\mathbb{Z}$.

results.title: Riemann–Lebesgue lemma on the circle
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T > 0$ and let $\mu$ be the Haar probability measure on the circle $\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$. For every $\mu$-integrable function $f : \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{C}$, the Fourier coefficients $\hat f(n) = \int e^{-2\pi i n t / T} f(t)\,d\mu(t)$ tend to $0$ as $|n| \to \infty$, that is, along the cofinite filter on $\mathbb{Z}$.

results.title: Global existence and uniqueness for homogeneous linear ODEs
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a real Banach space, write $L(E)$ for the space of continuous linear maps $E \to E$ with the operator norm, let $B : \mathbb{R} \to L(E)$ be continuous, and let $t_0 \in \mathbb{R}$ and $x_0 \in E$. Then there is exactly one function $x : \mathbb{R} \to E$ with $x(t_0) = x_0$ such that $x$ is differentiable at every $t \in \mathbb{R}$ with $x'(t) = B(t)\,x(t)$.

results.title: Jacobi's formula when the derivative is a left multiple of the matrix

results.summary: Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$, let $A$ be a real $n \times n$ matrix, let $\Phi : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$, and let $t \in \mathbb{R}$. If $\Phi$ is differentiable at $t$ with $\Phi'(t) = A \Phi(t)$, then $s \mapsto \det \Phi(s)$ is differentiable at $t$ with derivative $\operatorname{tr}(A) \det \Phi(t)$.

results.title: First-letter complement of a word
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite list of natural numbers, a leading letter $2$ is replaced by the two letters $1, 1$, and two leading letters $1, 1$ are replaced by the single letter $2$; the empty list and every list beginning otherwise (with a letter other than $1$ or $2$, or with a $1$ not followed by another $1$) are left unchanged.

results.title: Mirror image with first-letter complement
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite list $A$ of natural numbers, the mirror image $A^r$ is obtained by reversing $A$ and then complementing the first letter: a leading $2$ of the reversed list becomes $1, 1$, two leading letters $1, 1$ become $2$, and any other list is left unchanged. For example $(1, 1, 2)^r = (1, 1, 1, 1)$ and $(1, 1, 2, 1, 1, 1, 1)^r = (2, 1, 1, 2, 1, 1)$.

results.title: Approximants of Cloitre's sequence

results.title: Run boundaries of a sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For sequences $s, b : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, $b$ marks the maximal runs of $s$ when $b(0) = 0$, $b$ is strictly increasing, $s$ is constant on each block $[b(n), b(n+1))$, and for every $n$ each value of $s$ on the block $[b(n), b(n+1))$ differs from each value of $s$ on the next block $[b(n+1), b(n+2))$.

results.title: Sum of a sequence over a run
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For sequences $s, b : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the $n$-th run sum is $\sum_{b(n) \le j < b(n+1)} s(j)$, the sum of $s$ over the block $[b(n), b(n+1))$; it is $0$ when $b(n+1) \le b(n)$.

results.title: Cloitre's self-describing property
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A sequence $s : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is self-describing in Cloitre's sense when there is a sequence $b : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $b(0) = 0$, $b$ strictly increasing, $s$ constant on each block $[b(n), b(n+1))$ and each value of $s$ on a block different from each value on the next block (so the blocks are the maximal runs of $s$), such that for every $n$, $2 s(n) = \sum_{b(n) \le j < b(n+1)} s(j)$.

results.title: Binary digit sum
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the binary digit sum $s(n)$ is the sum of the digits of $n$ in base $2$, that is, the number of ones in the binary expansion of $n$.

results.title: Binary digit sum of zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The binary digit sum of $0$ is $0$.

results.title: Binary digit sum of an even number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $k$, the binary digit sum of $2k$ equals the binary digit sum of $k$: doubling appends the binary digit $0$.

results.title: Binary digit sum of an odd number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $k$, the binary digit sum of $2k + 1$ is one more than the binary digit sum of $k$: the binary expansion of $2k + 1$ is that of $k$ followed by the digit $1$.

results.title: Binary digit sum of one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The binary digit sum of $1$ is $1$.

results.title: Digital binomial theorem over a commutative semiring
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $s(m)$ denote the binary digit sum of a natural number $m$. For every natural number $n$ and all elements $x$, $y$ of a commutative semiring, $(x + y)^{s(n)}$ equals the sum of $x^{s(m)} y^{s(n - m)}$ over all $m$ with $0 \le m \le n$ and $s(m) + s(n - m) = s(n)$.

results.title: Digital binomial theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $s(m)$ denote the binary digit sum of a natural number $m$. For every natural number $n$ and all elements $x$, $y$ of a commutative ring, $(x + y)^{s(n)}$ equals the sum of $x^{s(m)} y^{s(n - m)}$ over all $m$ with $0 \le m \le n$ and $s(m) + s(n - m) = s(n)$.

results.title: Reed-Solomon encoder
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a field $F$ and points $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1} \in F$, the encoding of a polynomial $p \in F[X]$ is the word $(p(\alpha_0), \dots, p(\alpha_{n-1}))$ in $F^n$.

results.title: Reed-Solomon encoder as a linear map
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a field $F$ and points $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1} \in F$, the $F$-linear map $F[X] \to F^n$ sending a polynomial $p$ to $(p(\alpha_0), \dots, p(\alpha_{n-1}))$.

results.title: Reed-Solomon code
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1} \in F$ and let $k$ be a natural number. The Reed-Solomon code $\mathrm{RS}(\alpha, k)$ is the linear code of length $n$ over $F$ consisting of the words $(p(\alpha_0), \dots, p(\alpha_{n-1}))$ for the polynomials $p \in F[X]$ of degree less than $k$.

results.title: Root count at distinct points
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1}$ be pairwise distinct elements of $F$, and let $p \in F[X]$ be a nonzero polynomial. Then the number of indices $i < n$ with $p(\alpha_i) = 0$ is at most the degree of $p$.

results.title: Nonzero Reed-Solomon codewords are heavy
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1} \in F$ be pairwise distinct and let $k \le n$. For every nonzero polynomial $p \in F[X]$ of degree less than $k$, the encoding $(p(\alpha_0), \dots, p(\alpha_{n-1}))$ has at least $n - k + 1$ nonzero coordinates.

results.title: The Reed-Solomon encoder is injective on low-degree polynomials
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1} \in F$ be pairwise distinct and let $k \le n$. If two polynomials $p, q \in F[X]$ of degree less than $k$ satisfy $p(\alpha_i) = q(\alpha_i)$ for every $i < n$, then $p = q$.

results.title: Dimension of a Reed-Solomon code
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1} \in F$ be pairwise distinct and let $k \le n$. The Reed-Solomon code of the points $\alpha$ with parameter $k$ has dimension $k$ over $F$.

results.title: Lower bound on the minimum distance of a Reed-Solomon code
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1} \in F$ be pairwise distinct and let $k \in \mathbb{N}$. The Reed-Solomon code of the points $\alpha$ with parameter $k$ has minimum distance at least $\max(n - k, 0) + 1$.

results.title: A low-weight Reed-Solomon codeword
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1} \in F$ (not necessarily distinct) and let $1 \le k \le n$. There is a nonzero polynomial $p \in F[X]$ of degree less than $k$ whose encoding $(p(\alpha_0), \dots, p(\alpha_{n-1}))$ has at most $n - k + 1$ nonzero coordinates.

results.title: Reed-Solomon codes are MDS
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field (not necessarily finite), let $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1} \in F$ be pairwise distinct and let $1 \le k \le n$. The Reed-Solomon code of the points $\alpha$ with parameter $k$ has minimum distance exactly $n - k + 1$.

results.title: Reed-Solomon codes meet the Singleton bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite field, let $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1} \in F$ be pairwise distinct and let $1 \le k \le n$. The Reed-Solomon code $C$ of the points $\alpha$ with parameter $k$ has minimum distance $d = n - \dim C + 1$, so the Singleton bound $d \le n - \dim C + 1$ for linear codes holds with equality.

results.title: Berlekamp-Welch key equations
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1} \in F$, let $k, e \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $y \in F^n$ be a received word. A pair of polynomials $(Q, E)$ over $F$ solves the key equations for $y$ when $E$ is monic of degree $e$, $Q$ has degree less than $e + k$, and $Q(\alpha_i) = y_i E(\alpha_i)$ for every $i < n$.

results.title: The key equations are solvable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1} \in F$ and let $p \in F[X]$ have degree less than $k$. If a received word $y \in F^n$ differs from the encoding $(p(\alpha_0), \dots, p(\alpha_{n-1}))$ in at most $e$ coordinates, then the Berlekamp-Welch key equations for $y$ with parameters $k$ and $e$ have a solution $(Q, E)$.

results.title: Solver for the key equations
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: For a field $F$, points $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1} \in F$ and parameters $k, e \in \mathbb{N}$, a solver for the Berlekamp-Welch key equations is a procedure that takes a received word $y \in F^n$ and either returns a pair of polynomials $(Q, E)$ over $F$ or reports failure, such that every returned pair solves the key equations for $y$, and a pair is returned whenever the key equations for $y$ have a solution.
